q: The 'natural greenhouse effect' of the earth is caused by:
options: The heat generated by the volcanoes
The compression of the atmosphere by the weight of the oceans
The presence of the greenhouse gases in the atmosphere that trap the outgoing infrared radiation
The reflection of the sunlight by the clouds
explanation: The natural greenhouse effect is caused by the greenhouse gases of the atmosphere, mainly the carbon dioxide, the water vapour and the methane, that trap a part of the outgoing long wave radiation and keep the earth warm enough for life.

q: The 'photochemical smog' that occurs in the cities:
options: Is formed by the photochemical reaction between the nitrogen oxides and the hydrocarbons in the presence of the sunlight
Is the result of the fog of the winter that mixes with the smoke of the chimneys
Is the same as the sulphur dioxide smog of the industrial towns
Is caused by the dust storms of the arid regions
explanation: The photochemical smog is the oxidising smog that is formed by the photochemical reaction of the nitrogen oxides and the hydrocarbons in the presence of the sunlight, and it contains the ozone, the PAN and the aldehydes, while the sulphur dioxide smog of London is a reducing smog.

q: The 'sewage treatment' in India:
options: Is a chemical process in which the chlorine is added to the water
Is a biological process in which the bacteria break down the organic matter of the sewage
Is a physical process of the filtration of the sewage through the sand beds
Uses the aerobic and the anaerobic processes followed by the secondary and the tertiary treatment for the reuse of the treated water
explanation: The sewage treatment is a combination of the primary, the secondary and the tertiary stages, in which the primary treatment removes the solids, the secondary treatment uses the aerobic and the anaerobic bacterial action and the tertiary treatment polishes the water for the reuse in the industry and the agriculture.

q: The 'Refuse Derived Fuel' and the 'Waste to Energy' plants in India:
options: Produce the fuel from the agricultural residues for the industries
Burn the segregated combustible fraction of the municipal solid waste to generate the electricity and the bottom ash that is used in the construction
Compost the mixed municipal solid waste in the sanitary landfill
Convert the sewage sludge into the biogas for the rural households
explanation: The Refuse Derived Fuel and the Waste to Energy plants burn the segregated combustible fraction of the municipal solid waste to generate the electricity, and the residual bottom ash and the fly ash are used in the construction of the roads, the bricks and the landfill cover.

q: The 'mariculture' refers to:
options: The trade of the marine products in the international markets
The farming of the marine and the brackish water species of fish, the shrimps and the molluscs
The capture of the fish in the open sea with the trawlers
The processing of the fish in the cold storage units
explanation: Mariculture is the cultivation of the marine and the brackish water species of the fish, the shrimps, the mussels, the oysters and the seaweeds, and it complements the capture fisheries in meeting the growing demand of the seafood.

q: The 'Turtle Excluder Devices' in the fishing nets are used to:
options: Mark the nets of the fishing trawlers
Measure the size of the fish that is caught
Allow the escape of the sea turtles while retaining the shrimp and the small fish
Prevent the entry of the jellyfish into the nets
explanation: The Turtle Excluder Devices are fitted in the trawl nets so that the sea turtles escape from the nets while the shrimp and the small fish are retained, and their use is mandatory for the trawlers in the notified areas.

q: The 'coral bleaching' of 2016 and 2017 affected:
options: Large parts of the reefs of the Indian Ocean and the Pacific, and it was driven by the warming of the sea
Only the reefs of the Gulf of Mannar
The mangrove forests of the Sundarbans
The seagrass meadows of the Palk Bay
explanation: The mass coral bleaching event of 2016 and 2017 affected a large part of the reefs of the Indian and the Pacific Oceans, and it was driven by the anomalous warming of the sea, which causes the corals to expel the symbiotic algae that give them their colour.

q: The 'dugong' of the Gulf of Mannar and the Gulf of Kachchh:
options: Is a large fish that is caught for the oil
Is the juvenile of the green sea turtle
Is a crustacean that is farmed in the coastal areas
Is a vulnerable marine mammal that feeds on the seagrasses and the is listed in the Schedule I of the Wildlife Act
explanation: The dugong is a marine mammal that grazes on the seagrasses of the shallow seas and it is listed in the Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, and the population of the species in the Indian seas is small and threatened.

q: The 'National Biogas Programme' of India:
options: Promotes the setting up of the family type biogas plants for the rural households and the crop residue based plants
Promotes the anaerobic digestion of the sewage sludge in the cities
Supports the production of the compressed natural gas from the coal mine methane
Funds the setting up of the gasification plants of the biomass in the villages
explanation: The National Biogas Programme aims at the promotion of the family type biogas plants, of the crop residue based biogas plants and of the community plants, with the objective of providing the clean cooking fuel to the rural households and of the organic manure to the fields.

q: The 'Jaisalmer Solar Park' of the NTPC:
options: Is located in the Thar desert of Rajasthan near the Bhadla park
Is a 100 MW solar thermal plant commissioned in 2013 with the solar salt technology for the storage of the heat
Is the largest photovoltaic park of the country
Was set up for the electrolysis of the water for the green hydrogen
explanation: The Jaisalmer solar park of the NTPC in the Thar desert of Rajasthan is a 100 MW solar thermal plant that was commissioned in 2013, and it uses the molten salt technology for the storage of the heat, so that the plant can run after the sunset.

q: The 'round the clock' solar projects in India:
options: Are the solar parks that operate only during the daylight hours
Are the rooftop plants of the government buildings
Are the solar thermal plants of the Jaisalmer type
Combine the solar and the wind or the storage so that the plant supplies the power through the day and the night
explanation: The round the clock solar projects combine the solar and the wind capacity with the storage so that the electricity can be supplied throughout the day and the night, and the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy has planned such projects for the renewable rich states.

q: The 'Schedule II' of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 contains:
options: The species that are completely protected from any hunting or killing
The list of the protected areas of the country
The species that are protected but the hunting of which is permitted in a limited manner
The plants that are protected in the country
explanation: The Schedule I of the Wildlife Act contains the species that are fully protected, the Schedule II lists the species that are protected but the hunting of which is permitted in a limited manner, and the Schedule III lists the plants that are protected.

q: The 'Biodiversity Boards' at the state level:
options: Are the appellate authorities for the orders of the National Green Tribunal
Are the bodies that certify the organic farming of the state
Are the bodies that implement the Biological Diversity Act in the states and they have to be consulted for the access to the biological resources
Are the bodies that decide the compensation for the forest diversion
explanation: The State Biodiversity Boards are the bodies that implement the Biological Diversity Act in the states, and the biodiversity of the state and the local bodies has to be consulted for the access to the biological resources and for the commercial use of the biological resources.

q: The 'consent to establish and to operate' by the state pollution control board:
options: Is the registration of the unit for the air quality monitoring
Is the mandatory environmental clearance that a polluting unit must have before it starts the operations
Is a certificate for the rainwater harvesting of the industrial unit
Is the licence of the hazardous waste handling unit
explanation: The consent to establish and the consent to operate under the Water Act and the Air Act are the environmental clearances that a unit must obtain from the state pollution control board before it starts the operations and for the compliance of the standards of the emissions.

q: The 'Integrated Flood Management Programme' of India:
options: Works with the river basin organisations and the state governments for the flood management and the flood plain management
Is the scheme for the construction of the large dams
Is the programme for the river linking projects
Is the scheme for the desiltation of the canals of the irrigation departments
explanation: The Integrated Flood Management Programme works with the basin organisations, the state governments and the communities for the flood management, the flood plain management, the improvement of the flood forecasting and the capacity building of the flood management professionals.

q: The 'Drought Management Plan' of a state in India:
options: Is a document of the central government for the drought relief funds
Is a plan of the command area development for the irrigation works
Is the cropping pattern that the state follows in a drought year
Is prepared by the state government and it lists the drought prone blocks with the drought severity indices and the contingency plan
explanation: Every state government prepares a drought management plan that lists the drought prone blocks on the basis of the drought severity index, the historical rainfall and the vulnerability, and it also contains the contingency plan for the drought response.

q: The 'Clean Development Mechanism' of the Kyoto Protocol:
options: Provides for the trading of the emission allowances inside the European Union
Allows the industrialised countries to invest in the emission reduction projects in the developing countries and to earn the certified emission reduction units
Requires the developing countries to reduce their emissions by five per cent from the 1990 levels
Sets the binding targets for the developed countries only
explanation: The Clean Development Mechanism of the Kyoto Protocol allows the countries with the binding targets to invest in the emission reduction projects in the developing countries and to earn the certified emission reduction units against their commitments, while the Joint Implementation and the emissions trading are the other two mechanisms.

q: The '100 billion dollars a year' climate finance commitment:
options: Was the pledge of the developing countries to the developed nations
Was the fund that the World Bank provides for the adaptation in the small island states
Was the budget of the Green Climate Fund for its first decade
Was made by the developed countries to the developing countries and was reaffirmed at the COP29 at Baku in 2024 with a new collective quantified goal of 300 billion dollars
explanation: The developed countries had committed in 2009 to the mobilisation of 100 billion dollars a year by 2020 for the climate finance, and at the COP29 in Baku in 2024 this was replaced by the new collective quantified goal of at least 300 billion dollars a year by 2035.

q: The 'Biopiracy' in the context of the biodiversity refers to:
options: The use of the pesticides that kill the non target species
The release of the genetically modified crops in the environment
The commercial appropriation of the biological knowledge and the genetic resources of a community by a corporation without a fair share of the benefits to the community
The illegal trade of the endangered species across the borders
explanation: Biopiracy is the commercial appropriation of the traditional knowledge and the genetic resources of a community by a corporation without a fair share of the benefits reaching the community, and the case of the turmeric patent that was revoked in 1997 is the classic illustration.

q: The 'Ageratina adenophora' and the 'Lantana camara' are:
options: The invasive alien species of the forest lands of India that crowd out the native vegetation
The endangered medicinal plants of the Western Ghats
The mangrove species that restore the coastal belt
The exotic timber species that are planted in the social forestry plantations
explanation: The Ageratina adenophora, the crofton weed, and the Lantana camara are the invasive alien species that have invaded the forest lands of India and that crowd out the native vegetation, and the Parthenium hysterophorus is a similar menace for the pastures and the crops.

q: The 'Grasses and the herbs of the alpine meadow' in the Western Himalaya:
options: Are the natural grasslands of the Deccan that support the buffaloes
Are the shola grasslands of the Western Ghats
Are the 'bugyal' communities that the Van Gujjar herds of the high Himalaya use as the summer grazing grounds
Are the mangrove communities of the deltas
explanation: The bugyals are the high altitude natural grasslands of the Himalaya that provide the summer grazing grounds for the Van Gujjar and the Bakarwal herds, and they are a typical example of the fragile alpine ecosystem that is highly vulnerable to the overgrazing.

q: The patches of the forest that are:
options: The reserve forests of the state governments notified under the Forest Act
The plantations of the medicinal plants in the tribal areas
The community forests that are leased out for the timber
The patches of the forest that are protected by the local communities because of the religious beliefs attached to them
explanation: The sacred groves are the forest patches that the local communities protect because of the religious beliefs attached to them, and they are found in the states of Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Goa and Rajasthan, and many of them are notified as the protected areas.

q: The 'Van Panchayats' in the hills of Uttarakhand:
options: Are the committees of the panchayat for the watershed development
Are the traditional forest management institutions of the villages that protect the local forests and the grazing lands
Are the committees of the forest department for the patrolling
Are the revenue villages of the hill administration
explanation: The Van Panchayats are the traditional institutions of the village forest management in the hills of Uttarakhand that protect the forests, the grazing lands and the village commons under the customary rights, and they are the antecedents of the forest protection committees.

q: The 'Bhagwan Sree Bird Sanctuary' of Gujarat:
options: Is a protected area of the wetlands of the Nal that is the only permanent habitat of the Greater Flamingo in the country
Is the wetland of the Keoladeo that hosts the Siberian cranes
Is the lagoon of the Rajasthan that is a Ramsar site of the wetlands
Is the sanctuary of the Punjab that is the home of the blackbuck
explanation: The Bhagwan Sree Bird Sanctuary, also called the Nal Sarovar, in the Ahmedabad district of Gujarat is the only permanent habitat of the Greater Flamingo in the country, and the Nal and the adjoining areas were notified as a Ramsar site in 2021.

q: The 'Nalsarovar' of Gujarat and the 'Keoladeo' of Rajasthan:
options: Are the nesting grounds of the marine turtles of the Arabian Sea
Are the mangrove sanctuaries of the Gulf of Kachchh
Are both the wetlands of the Ramsar network and are the wintering grounds of the migratory water birds
Are the only salt pans of the country
explanation: The Nalsarovar of Gujarat and the Keoladeo of Rajasthan are both part of the Ramsar network and they are among the most important wintering grounds of the migratory water birds of the Central Asian flyway in India.

q: The 'Point Calimere Wildlife Sanctuary' of Tamil Nadu:
options: Is a marine sanctuary of the Gulf of Mannar
Is a coastal sanctuary with the largest congregation of the flamingos in Tamil Nadu and it is a Ramsar site
Is a forest sanctuary of the Western Ghats for the lion-tailed macaque
Is a bird sanctuary of the wetlands of the Kaveri
explanation: The Point Calimere Wildlife Sanctuary, along with the adjoining the Vedaranyam and the Koonthankulam, forms a Ramsar site and it has the largest congregation of the flamingos in Tamil Nadu, with the great white pelican and the black-headed ibis among the birds that are found here.

q: The 'Ecotourism' in the protected areas of India:
options: Is permitted only in the the tiger reserves of the central India
Has been banned by the Supreme Court in the sensitive areas
Is the basis of the revenue of the state governments in the hill states
Is promoted by the National Tourism and the Forest Departments as a means of the conservation finance and the livelihood of the local communities
explanation: The ecotourism is promoted in the protected areas as a means of generating the conservation finance and of providing the livelihoods to the local communities, and the eco-development plans of the Project Tiger reserves are the classic example of the community based ecotourism.

q: The 'Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022' of India:
options: Added the four species of the carnivores to the Schedule I and strengthened the protection of the habitats
Reduced the penalties for the wildlife poaching
Removed the provisions of the forest rights of the communities
Created the National Green Tribunal
explanation: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act of 2022 added the four species of the carnivores, the leopard, the snow leopard, the cheetah and the jungle cat, to the Schedule I, strengthened the protection of the habitats and the live capture and increased the penalties for the offences.

q: The 'Project Vulture' of the Bombay Natural History Society:
options: Was a project for the release of the flamingos in the Nal Sarovar
Was the project for the reintroduction of the cheetah in Namibia
Was the programme for the conservation of the crocodile in Bhitarkanika
Was launched in the 1990s to bring back the two species of the vultures that had declined because of the diclofenac
explanation: Project Vulture was launched in the 1990s by the Bombay Natural History Society to bring back the white-backed and the long-billed vultures that had disappeared because of the veterinary drug diclofenac, and the ban of the drug in 2006 helped in the recovery of the populations.

q: The 'Bombay Natural History Society':
options: Is the organisation that publishes the State of the Forest Report
Was founded in 1883 and has been at the forefront of the research and the conservation of the birds and the wildlife of India
Was founded in 1958 to protect the tigers of the central India
Is the body that runs the the national parks of the northeastern states
explanation: The Bombay Natural History Society, founded in 1883, has been at the forefront of the research and the conservation of the birds of India and of the wildlife, and its bird census and the publication of the journal are among its well known activities.

q: The 'National Biodiversity Day' of India is observed on:
options: 19 December, the day of the adoption of the Convention on Biological Diversity
2 February, the day of the wetland convention
22 April, the day of the Earth Day
5 June, the day of the World Environment Day
explanation: The National Biodiversity Day of India is observed on 19 December, the day of the adoption of the Convention on Biological Diversity at Rio de Janeiro in 1992, and it was first observed in the country in 2019.

q: The 'National Cleanup Day' of India is observed on:
options: 5 June, the day of the World Environment Day
21 March, the day of the International Day of Forests
1 October, the day of the launch of the Swachh Bharat Mission
2 October, the day of the Gandhi Jayanti
explanation: The National Cleanup Day is observed on 1 October across the country as part of the Swachh Bharat Mission, with the large scale cleanliness drives that are organised at the rivers, the coasts, the railways and the tourist places.

q: The 'Green Credit Programme' of India:
options: Is a market based mechanism that gives a tradable credit for the tree plantation on the degraded forest land
Is a subsidy for the farmers who use the organic manure
Is a certificate for the rooftop solar installation
Is a credit guarantee for the green finance of the startups
explanation: The Green Credit Programme is a market based mechanism in which the participants that plant the trees on the degraded forest land earn the green credits, which are tradable to meet the obligations of the tree plantation under the compensatory afforestation.

q: The 'National Afforestation Programme' of India:
options: Was launched in 1997 with the plantation of the trees on the wastelands of the drought prone areas
Is the programme of the plantation on the community lands of the Panchayats
Is the programme of the mangrove restoration of the coastal states
Was launched in 2000 with the objective of the afforestation of the degraded forest lands and the augmentation of the forest cover
explanation: The National Afforestation Programme was launched in 2000 with the objective of the afforestation of the degraded forest lands, the augmentation of the forest cover and the improvement of the productivity of the forests, and it is implemented through the forest departments of the states.

q: The 'Integrated Scheme for the management of the coastal zones' in India:
options: Was started in 2017 with the launch of the National Marine Fisheries Policy
Was started in 2005 with the creation of the National Green Tribunal
Was started in 2010 with the World Bank support for the demonstration projects of the Integrated Coastal Zone Management
Was started in 1991 with the notification of the coastal regulation zones
explanation: The Integrated Scheme for the management of the coastal zones was started in 2010 with the World Bank support for the demonstration projects of the Integrated Coastal Zone Management, and it was later renamed as the Integrated Scheme for the management of the coastal zones.

q: The 'National Marine Protected Area' network of India:
options: Is the network of the coastal zone regulation authorities
Comprises the Marine National Parks, the Marine Sanctuaries and the Biosphere Reserves of the coastal and the marine areas
Is limited to the Marine National Parks that are under the Wildlife Act
Is a network of the fishing harbours of the states
explanation: The national marine protected area network of India comprises the Marine National Parks, the Marine Sanctuaries and the Marine Biosphere Reserves, and the framework of the network is the National Marine Protected Area Network with the target of the ecologically representative and the connected system of the marine protected areas.

q: The 'Sagar Island' of West Bengal:
options: Is the site of the Hatiya island of the Brahmaputra
Is the volcanic island of the Nicobar district
Is the site of the Sagar cyclone of 2020 and the Ambujapur and the Ganga heritage site
Is the largest sand island of the Bay of Bengal with the mud volcanoes of the Baratpurjhati
explanation: Sagar Island in the South 24 Parganas district of West Bengal is the largest of the sand islands of the Bay of Bengal, and it is known for the mud volcanoes of the Baratpurjhati, while the cyclone of the same name hit the island in 2020.

q: The 'Oil spill' of the MV Wakashio off the Seychelles in 2020:
options: Raised the concerns over the preparedness of the coastal states for the marine oil spill response
Was the first oil spill in the Indian Ocean
Was caused by the collision with the reef off the Andaman Islands
Led to the ban on the maritime traffic of the Indian Ocean
explanation: The grounding of the MV Wakashio off the Seychelles in 2020, when about 80,000 tonnes of the fuel oil was spilled, raised the concerns over the preparedness of the coastal states of India for the marine oil spill response, since the coastline is a sensitive habitat.

q: The 'National Water Policy, 2012' of India:
options: Prescribes the water sharing among the states through the river boards
Provides for the bunding of the minor irrigation tanks
Recommends the minimum quantity of water that should be assured to every household and the prioritisation of the drinking water over the other uses
Fixes the water rates of the urban local bodies
explanation: The National Water Policy of 2012 recommends the minimum quantity of water that should be assured to every household and it prioritises the drinking water over the other uses, and it also recommends the linking of the water development projects and the participatory management of the water.

q: The 'Central Ground Water Authority' of India:
options: Certifies the bore wells for the irrigation wells
Regulates the development and the use of the ground water and it has been notified as a groundwater authority under the 2023 rules
Regulates the extraction of the ground water in the mining areas
Controls the pollution of the ground water in the industrial clusters
explanation: The Central Ground Water Authority was constituted in 2019 to regulate the development and the use of the ground water in the country and the Central Ground Water Rules of 2021 were notified to permit the regulation of the extraction in the over-exploited and the critically over-exploited blocks.

q: The 'Bhakra Nangal' and the 'Sardar Sarovar' projects are the:
options: The flood control projects of the eastern India
The irrigation projects of the command area development programme
The river valley projects that have been a part of the Green Revolution and of the drinking water supply
The inter-state river dispute projects
explanation: The Bhakra Nangal and the Sardar Sarovar are the river valley projects that have provided the irrigation and the drinking water to millions of people and have been a part of the Green Revolution, and both of them were the subject of the inter-state disputes.

q: The 'Ganga and the Yamuna' as the 'National Waterways' declared by the Parliament:
options: Are National Waterway 1 and National Waterway 2 respectively
Are National Waterway 2 and National Waterway 3 respectively
Are National Waterway 3 and National Waterway 1 respectively
Are not among the declared national waterways
explanation: The Ganga and the Bhagirathi is the National Waterway 1 and the Brahmaputra is the National Waterway 2, while the West Coast Canal with the Kollam and the Kottayam route is the National Waterway 3, and the Sagar and the Narmada is the National Waterway 4.

q: The 'Regulation of the aquaculture' in the coastal states of India is done under the:
options: Marine Fisheries Act of 1969
Water Act of 1974
Biological Diversity Act of 2002
Coastal Aquaculture Management Rules of 1980 and the Coastal (Aquaculture) Rules of 1991
explanation: The aquaculture in the coastal areas is regulated under the Coastal Aquaculture Management Rules of 1980 and the Coastal (Aquaculture) Rules of 1991, which prescribe the norms for the brackish water farming and the no-areas for the shrimp culture.

q: The 'Atoll' and the 'Lagoon' differ in that:
options: Both are the coral islands of the Indian Ocean
An atoll has a ring of the coral reefs enclosing a lagoon, while a lagoon is the shallow body of the water that is enclosed by the reef
A lagoon is formed on the continental shelf and an atoll in the deep sea
An atoll is a volcanic island and a lagoon is a coral island
explanation: An atoll is a ring of the coral reefs that encloses a lagoon, and a lagoon is the shallow body of the water that is surrounded by the reef, and the atolls of the Lakshadweep and of the Maldives are the classic examples.

q: The 'El Nino' years are associated in India with:
options: A higher incidence of the cyclones in the Bay of Bengal
A reduction in the salinity of the Arabian Sea
A weaker monsoon and a higher probability of the drought in the sub-tropical regions
A stronger monsoon over the western coast
explanation: In the El Nino years, the warming of the equatorial Pacific alters the pattern of the atmospheric circulation, the subsidence over the Indian region increases and the monsoon weakens, which raises the probability of the drought in the sub-tropical latitudes.

q: The 'Black carbon' that is deposited on the Himalayan snow:
options: Accelerates the melting of the snow because it absorbs the solar radiation and reduces the albedo
Increases the albedo of the snow and slows the melting
Is the cause of the winter rainfall of the Western Himalaya
Is the source of the blue ice of the glaciers
explanation: The deposition of the black carbon on the Himalayan snow reduces the albedo of the snow and absorbs the solar radiation, which accelerates the melting of the glaciers and the snow and contributes to the water stress of the Himalayan rivers.

q: The 'National Solar Mission' of India was also known as:
options: The National Solar Policy of 2011
The Solar India Programme of 2015
The Rooftop Solar Programme of 2019
The Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission of 2022
explanation: The National Solar Mission of India, the Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission, was launched in 2022 and it succeeded the National Solar Mission of 2011 with the target of adding about 300 GW of the solar capacity by 2030-31.

q: The 'Biodiversity Register' of a state:
options: Is the register of the species that are listed in the Schedule I of the Wildlife Act
Is a public record of the species of the state that is maintained by the state biodiversity board for the access and the benefit sharing
Is the list of the protected areas of the state
Is the register of the traditional knowledge holders of the tribal communities
explanation: The Biodiversity Register is a public record of the species of the state that is maintained by the state biodiversity board, and it is the base for the appraisal of the applications for the access to the biological resources and for the sharing of the benefits.

q: The 'National Guidelines for the Management of the Crops Residues' in India:
options: Provide for the subsidy on the machinery for the collection of the residues
Promote the happy seeder and the mulching and the incorporation of the residues in the soil to prevent the burning in the fields
Ban the use of the crop residues as the fuel in the houses of the villages
Prescribe the sale of the residues in the market at a fixed price
explanation: The National Guidelines for the Management of the Crop Residues promote the in-situ management through the happy seeder, the mulching and the incorporation of the residues in the soil, and the customised machinery, so as to prevent the burning of the stubble in the fields.

q: The 'National Air Quality Index' of the Central Pollution Control Board:
options: Has been prepared by the India Meteorological Department
Is the index of the pollution of the water bodies of the country
Has eight pollutants, including the PM2.5, the PM10, the NO2, the NH3, the SO2, the CO, the ozone and the lead, and it has six categories
Has only the PM2.5 and the PM10 as the pollutants
explanation: The National Air Quality Index was launched by the Central Pollution Control Board in October 2014 with eight pollutants, including the PM2.5, the PM10, the nitrogen dioxide, the ammonia, the sulphur dioxide, the carbon monoxide, the ozone and the lead, and it classifies the air quality in the six categories from the good to the severe.

q: The 'National Commission for the Protection of the Child Rights' of India:
options: Runs the juvenile justice courts of the states
Supervises the adoption of the children by the foreign nationals
Certifies the child friendly schools of the states
Monitors the violations of the rights of the children and it is the appellate body for the complaints about the violations of the Right to Education
explanation: The National Commission for the Protection of the Child Rights monitors the violations of the rights of the children, and it is also the appellate body for the complaints about the violations of the Right to Education, in addition to the state commissions.

q: The 'Suryakanya' and the 'Poshan 2.0' schemes of India:
options: Are the supplementary nutrition programmes that deal with the maternal and the child nutrition of the vulnerable groups
Are the schemes for the electrification of the rural households
Are the schemes for the digital literacy of the rural women
Are the urban housing schemes of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
explanation: The Integrated Child Nutrition Services scheme of the government has two components, the Supplementary Nutrition Programme of the urban areas called Poshan 2.0 and the rural one called Suryakanya, and both are aimed at the improvement of the nutrition of the children, the pregnant women and the lactating mothers.

q: National River Conservation Plan aims:
options: Is the programme for the linking of the rivers
Is the plan for the flood control of the Brahmaputra
Is the plan for the irrigation of the command areas of the dams
Aims at the pollution abatement of the rivers and at the treatment of the sewage that is generated in the urban agglomerations of the river basins
explanation: The National River Conservation Plan aims at the pollution abatement of the rivers, at the treatment of the sewage that is generated in the urban agglomerations of the river basins and at the setting up of the the river conservation works, and the Ganga Action Plan and the Yamuna Action Plan are its main components.

q: The 'Namami Gange Programme':
options: Is the programme of the development of the tourism on the riverfront
Is an integrated programme of the sewage treatment, the river surface cleaning, the riverfront development and the biodiversity and the afforestation
Is the programme of the construction of the dams on the Ganga
Is the programme of the development of the irrigation in the Ganga basin
explanation: The Namami Gange Programme is an integrated programme with the components of the sewage treatment, the river surface cleaning, the riverfront development, the biodiversity and the afforestation, the river conservation and the afforestation, the monitoring and the public awareness, and it was renamed as the Jal Jeevan Mission of the Ganga in 2019.

q: The 'National Green Development Mission' or the 'Green Mission' of India:
options: Aims at the greening of the urban areas and at the pollution control with the help of the public participation
Is the mission for the afforestation of the degraded forests
Is the programme for the conservation of the tigers
Is the mission for the clean cooking in the rural households
explanation: The National Green Development Mission, the Green Mission, was launched to improve the green cover of the urban areas, to control the pollution with the public participation and to develop the green belts around the industries, and it also seeks the involvement of the corporate sector and the NGOs.

q: The 'Per capita carbon emissions' of India:
options: Are equal to the global average because of the rapid industrialisation
Have been rising faster than the emissions of the developed countries since 2015
Are among the lowest in the world, well below the global average, because of the large population and the low per capita energy consumption
Are the highest in the world because of the coal based power plants
explanation: The per capita carbon emissions of India are among the lowest in the world and well below the global average, because of the low per capita energy consumption of a large population, even though the total emissions of the country have risen sharply with the industrialisation.

q: The dyeing units of the textile clusters of Rajasthan are a cause of concern because of:
options: the desertification of the agricultural land
the depletion of the ozone layer
the water pollution of the rivers and the ground water
the depletion of the soil salinity
explanation: The dyeing and the bleaching units of the textile clusters of the Rajasthan discharge the untreated effluents, and this is a cause of the water pollution of the rivers and the ground water in the clusters of the Bhilwara, the Jaipur and the Pali.

q: The 'Mission on Climate Change' of the 'National Action Plan on Climate Change':
options: Is limited to the adaptation in the coastal states
Includes the eight missions, of which the National Solar Mission and the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture are among the most important
Includes only the National Mission on the afforestation
Covers only the urban transport and the buildings
explanation: The National Action Plan on Climate Change has eight missions, of which the National Solar Mission and the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture are among the most important, and they are complemented by the climate specific national missions.

q: The 'Waste to Wealth' approach of the Swachh Bharat Mission:
options: Burns the mixed waste in the open pits
Buries the waste in the sanitary landfills of the cities
Sells the waste to the cement kilns only
Converts the biodegradable waste into the manure and the plastic waste into the fuel and the construction material
explanation: The Waste to Wealth approach of the Swachh Bharat Mission seeks to convert the biodegradable waste into the manure through the compost and the vermicompost, and the plastic waste into the fuel, the refuelling and the construction material, so that the waste becomes a resource instead of a burden.

q: The 'Karnataka' and the 'Tamil Nadu' of India:
options: Have the largest number of the power plants that run on the biomass and the bagasse cogeneration
Are the leading exporters of the sea fish
Have the largest area under the mangroves
Are the only states with the solar parks
explanation: Karnataka and Tamil Nadu have the largest number of the cogeneration plants that run on the biomass and the bagasse, and this is the result of the large number of the sugar mills and of the industries that have set up the captive power plants.
